title: Evolutionary Cohabitation
definition: The concept that long-term predator-prey relationships can evolve into a stable, symbiotic cohabitation under specific conditions of temporal depth and host survival.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a long-term relationship between two animals where each learns to adapt to the other. Over time, this can lead to a stable arrangement where both benefit, much like a house-sharing situation.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Evolutionary cohabitation theory suggests that long-term, non-lethal predation can transform into a form of symbiosis through reciprocal co-adaptation. This involves host physiological changes and predator evaluative memory based on various host characteristics.
difficulty_levels.expert: This concept expands the field of co-evolutionary biology to include chronic, host-parasite interactions with cognitive predators. It highlights the evolution of cognitive processes in predators and the physiological adaptations in hosts, leading to a stable, long-term relationship that benefits both parties.

extra_fields.insight: The evolutionary cohabitation theory introduces a new perspective on long-term predator-prey relationships, suggesting that they can evolve into stable, symbiotic cohabitations under specific conditions.
